message.content:
In Texas, tenants have several statutory protections and responsibilities under the Texas Property Code and related laws. Below is an overview of key rights and obligations you should know: | Category | Key Rights | Key Responsibilities | |----------|------------|-----------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent (or two if the lease is for a furnished unit).
• Must return deposit within 30 days after lease ends, minus deductions for damages beyond normal wear & tear. | • Keep records of the condition of the unit at move‑in and move‑out. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary, and livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity).
• Tenants can withhold rent or repair & deduct if landlord fails to comply. | • Report needed repairs promptly; keep written records. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord cannot enter without notice (except emergencies) or harass you.
• Notice required: 24 hours for non‑emergency entries. | • Respect landlord’s right to inspect for maintenance or show the unit to prospective renters. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease must be in writing if it lasts longer than one year.
• Landlord cannot impose unreasonable restrictions (e.g., banning pets unless justified). | • Sign only what you understand; negotiate terms before signing. | | **Rent Increases** | • For month‑to‑month leases, landlord must give 30 days’ notice before raising rent.
• For fixed‑term leases, rent can’t change until the lease expires. | • Review lease renewal clauses; negotiate changes if possible. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (including public assistance). | • Provide necessary documentation (e.g., proof of income) in a nondiscriminatory manner. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must follow the proper legal process: serve a written notice (e.g., 3‑day notice for nonpayment), file a lawsuit, obtain a court order, then sheriff’s eviction.
• You have the right to contest the eviction in court. | • Respond to notices promptly; attend court hearings. | | **Repair & Deduct** | • If landlord fails to fix major problems, you may repair them yourself and deduct costs from rent (up to $500 per month). | • Keep receipts and document the issue. | | **Right to Privacy** | • Landlord must respect your privacy; they can’t conduct surveillance or tamper with personal belongings. | • Secure your personal items; report any unauthorized access. | | **Utilities** | • Landlord must provide essential utilities (water, heat, electricity) unless otherwise specified. | • Pay utilities on time; notify landlord of outages. | | **Subletting & Assignment** | • Lease may restrict subletting; if allowed, you must get landlord’s written consent. | • Follow lease terms when subletting; keep landlord informed. | ### Practical Steps to Protect Your Rights 1. **Read the Lease Carefully** – Understand all clauses, especially those about rent, deposits, repairs, and termination. 2. **Document Everything** – Take photos, keep written communication, and retain copies of all notices and receipts. 3. **Know the Law** – Familiarize yourself with the Texas Property Code sections relevant to your situation (e.g., §§ 92.001–92.021 for habitability). 4. **Communicate in Writing** – Whenever possible, use email or certified mail to keep a record of disputes or requests. 5. **Seek Legal Advice** – If you face eviction or a dispute, consult a local attorney or tenant advocacy group (e.g., Texas Tenants Union). If you have a specific scenario (e.g., landlord refusing to make repairs, dispute over security deposit, or potential discrimination), let me know and I can offer more tailored guidance.
